data.why: The interface bundles a 31,236-record ChEMBL IC50 subset selected by default; a small synthetic CSV matching its document/molecule/target/relation/value_nM/units/validity/year schema is also provided so the scientist can exercise the 'My file' upload path with exact values, right- and left-censored bounds, a missing value, a zero value and a flagged-validity record.

goals: Load the bundled IC50 dataset and quantify what share of weak-potency evidence is lost when an exact-value (pChEMBL-style) filter is applied
Fit a pooled censored-normal (Tobit) model and compare its weak-share and mean-potency estimates against the exact-values-only estimate
Fit a grouped (per-paper) censored-normal model and inspect the distribution of per-paper potency overstatement when bounds are dropped
Compare two targets (strata) pooled versus within-paper to check whether a pooled difference's sign survives when restricted to papers that measured both
Check whether a paper's reported bounds look like disguised ceilings by testing for tied top exact values
Upload a custom IC50 CSV or ChEMBL export and rerun the same audit on it

review.summary: The tree gets the tool's purpose right: what a pChEMBL-style exact-value filter removes, censored-model bias, and whether pooled comparisons hold within papers. Its phases match the page, and the nine screens I sampled support the nodes apart from the two flagged in evidence. It needs small fixes before filing: add the counter-screen finding from the README, add features for the tie test and by-role censoring, split the oversized censored-model feature, and correct the misleading t6 example and the t13 branch condition.
